title: A brace over two names covers only the first
body:
`brace` takes `over NAME` or `over ROW [N [M]]`. At `c846b14`, `brace { over a b; }` with two box names draws the brace under `a` alone, and acre gives no error.

The pipeline figure needed one brace under two neighbouring stage boxes, `cloud` and `align`, labelled with the function that runs both. `over cloud align` covered `cloud` only. The figure now gives the brace as `from 592 352; to 1108 352`, with each number worked out by hand from the boxes' widths and the stack's gap. Those numbers break when a box changes width.

## Proposal

- `over A B ...` spans the box around every named thing.
- A word after `over` that names nothing is an error, not a silent no-op.
close_reason: Landed in ebade49 on dev. `over` takes any number of things and the brace spans the box around them, following the first. A word that names nothing is an error. Test: `a_brace_over_several_names_spans_the_box_around_them`.
